proof_summary:
The congruences $2^{58}\equiv1\pmod{233}$, $2^{233}\equiv1\pmod{1399}$, and $2^{206}\equiv-3\pmod{1399}$ show that $1399$ divides every relevant term. The noncoverage assumptions give $n
ot\equiv2\pmod5$, $n
ot\equiv11\pmod{18}$, and $n
ot\equiv26\pmod{42}$; multiplicative-order periodicity then reduces divisibility by each prime below $1399$ to finite modular checks over residue classes of $n$, excluding them all (including $67,271,523$ via those three restrictions), so $1399$ is the least prime factor.
